notes: Cleanest discriminator: concrete SEO metadata. Both without-skill runs proposed only naming patterns (no actual title/description text per page) and failed that assertion; both with-skill runs shipped concrete pairs for every main page.

Assumptions discipline: the Spanish-rich baseline presented guesses as closed decisions (0 assumption markers, no reaction section). With-skill runs marked 15-25 assumptions inline and collected them for Mariana to react to. The sparse-English baseline only marked guesses because the prompt explicitly demanded it - the skill makes this behavior unconditional.

Non-discriminating assertions (passed in all 4 runs): plan file saved, correct language, phased roadmap, mapping to the real repo collections. A strong base model already does these; they remain as regression guards.
Cost of the skill: +19pt pass rate for roughly +10k tokens on the rich eval (61.8k vs 51.9k) and +3k on the sparse eval (64.4k vs 61.4k); wall-clock comparable.

Privacy observation: one baseline run mined a personal Gmail address out of git history and put it in the plan; the skill instead asks for her preferred contact method in the interview. Consider an explicit assertion for this.

Grader eval-feedback: make the repo-untouched assertion self-contained (per-run git snapshot); metrics assertion is ambiguous for the art project where metrics genuinely do not apply; no assertion checks factual accuracy of repo claims (all spot-checked claims happened to be accurate this round).
